page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc9i.8xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine within the high clock speed instance family. Built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6982P-C processor running at 3.4 GHz, the server delivers 32 dedicated virtual CPUs. The architecture implements a compute-heavy 1:2 resource ratio, providing 64.0 GB of total system memory, which allocates exactly 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

Hardware provisioning focuses entirely on raw CPU execution and high network throughput. The instance includes a 20 Gbps baseline network bandwidth allocation for internal and external traffic. It does not incorporate local storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes for all persistent file systems. There are no dedicated hardware graphics processing units bundled with the configuration, and complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not provided by default.

The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio and high 3.4 GHz base frequency make this server type cost-efficient for processor-bound tasks where large memory caches are unnecessary. Because users do not pay for idle memory capacity or unneeded local storage hardware, operational expenditure remains aligned with compute utilization. The primary architectural tradeoff is the absence of local disk IOPS, meaning disk operations rely entirely on attached cloud storage.

Appropriate workload fits for the Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc9i.8xlarge include compute-intensive batch processing, continuous integration and build pipelines, gaming server infrastructure, financial modeling, CPU-bound scientific simulations, and scalable web application backends requiring sustained high core clock speeds.
